title: Centralize escalation headline generation to prevent duplication across consumers
context: The "N need your call (+M for context)" headline was hand-copied into both the CLI and MCP tool, with matching dead prose. This duplication led to inconsistency — the VS Code panel missed applying the actionable filter because maintenance of the duplicated code was error-prone. Touches invariant(s): con_7217ab24ab (Regression guard: "Flaky test failure under parallelism: native tree-sitter module resolution race on Windows" must not recur.); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Extract `escalationHeadline()` function in src/core/escalations.ts that generates the headline once for all consumers (CLI, MCP, VS Code). Introduced `EscalationAudience` type ("cli" | "mcp") to customize wording while keeping logic centralized. All consumers now call this single function instead of maintaining their own copy.
consequences: Consistency guaranteed across all output consumers
Single source of truth for headline logic and wording
Non-actionable rows now uniformly distinguished ("·" glyph in CLI/MCP, neutral icon + "context only" in VS Code)
Easier future maintenance — headline changes require editing one function, not three places
VS Code panel can now correctly filter and display non-actionable entries
alternatives_rejected: Continue hand-copying headline logic per consumer (original approach, caused maintenance bugs)
Extract only to CLI, leave MCP/VS Code with separate implementations (partial solution, wouldn't fix inconsistency)
Create a shared config constant instead of a function (wouldn't handle audience-specific wording variations like "your call" vs "the human's call")
